residue.text: Retained stage1 residue: stable addressing cannot establish that a captured token matches intention. S2 gives K5/K7 equal score 75, with K5 first; score alone cannot identify K7. Comparing intact and corrupted tokens against the checklist before commit is a prevention hypothesis, still untested.

Retained INV concern: test mismatch-triggered extra refreshes enabled versus suppressed, using equal-duration inspection slots to preserve timing and snapshot eligibility. Independently inject or withhold mismatch notifications at matched gates; log requests separately from writes. These prospective interventions distinguish mismatch -> refresh from refresh -> mismatch. Recurrence requires a return refresh changing retained selection; extra requests alone do not establish feedback. Diagnostic miswrites fail the unchanged outcome.

Retained stage1 and ATT/INV limits: a no-refresh diagnostic after minute 2 cannot satisfy final freshness; completion candidates require final S2. No completed replay or repeated feedback is supplied. Real binding, detection, capture-error frequency and interruption costs remain unknown. Concurrent changes, deleted keys and load failures are outside scope; production connectors, macros, telemetry and usability participants are absent. Claims concern eight synthetic records only.

summary.text: Stage1 construction hypothesis: capture checklist keys as immutable tokens and resolve each at commit after refresh. Proposed nine-minute replay uses inspect/refresh/commit for K2 at 0-3, K5 at 3-6 and K7 at 6-9. Predicted writes are exactly K2/K5/K7, other statuses unchecked, scores read-only and final S2 loaded. Log times, tokens, intended/actual keys and final map; success is unobserved.

ATT/INV propose a separate necessity test: retain row binding and loaded S0; inspect/commit K2 at 0-2, K5 at 2-4 and K7 at 4-6, then refresh at 6-7. Hypothesis: fixed order yields only the target writes; key-persistent statuses survive final S2. Verified exact statuses, zero incorrect-key writes and seven-minute completion would refute per-commit refresh necessity within this model.

Stage1 second-attack hypothesis: keep the nine-minute migration schedule but replace intended K7 token with K5 after inspection at 6-7. Resolving that corrupted token predicts K5 written at 8-9 and K7 unchecked. Compare intact versus corrupted tokens to separate carrier stability from intention integrity; this diagnostic fails target correctness and is unexecuted.

O5 stipulates one wrong-target K5 write after selecting K2 and refreshing. INV proposes changing/frozen snapshots crossed with row/key binding under identical actions: only changing-plus-row predicts this miswrite. Both that controlled prediction and mismatch-refresh recurrence remain hypotheses; the single supplied trace establishes neither repeated feedback nor operational reliability.
